1. **Private key blocks (line 18):** the pattern used `[\s\S]*`, which grabs as much text as it can. So it ran to the end of the text, or past the next key block. Changing it to `[\s\S]*?` makes each match stop at its own `-----END … PRIVATE KEY-----`, or at the end of the output if the output was cut off. Text after the key now stays.
2. **URL passwords (line 64):** the replacement dropped the `@`, so `postgres://app:pw@db` became `postgres://app:[cedia:redacted]db`. It now puts the `@` back.
3. **Generic `sk-` keys (line 20):** the comment says generic token patterns need a digit, but this one didn't require one. So words like `sk-learn-and-more-words` were redacted. A lookahead now requires a digit.
4. **Secret-looking names (line 38):** `token` also matched `MAX_TOKENS`, and lines in `.env` format (`NAME=value`) redact any value. So `MAX_TOKENS=4096` was hidden. I changed it to `token(?!s|iz)`, which skips "tokens" and "tokenizer" names.

Fix 4 is my judgement call, not the only possible one. The trade-off is that a variable really named something like `ACCESS_TOKENS=…` would no longer be redacted. The alternative was to stop treating all-digit `.env` values as secrets, but the code's comment says `.env` lines count "any value". Tell me if you'd prefer that version.

I fixed four bugs in `redact.ts`, and `bun test` now passes: 4 tests, 0 failures. I didn't change the tests.

1. **Private key blocks:** the pattern used a greedy `[\s\S]*`. It ran on to the last END line in the output, or to the end of the text, so it swallowed text after the key and merged two keys into one match. I made it lazy (`[\s\S]*?`). A key whose output was cut off before its END line is still redacted to the end of the text.
2. **Passwords in URLs:** the replacement dropped the `@`, so `postgres://app:pw@db` became `postgres://app:[cedia:redacted]db`. It now puts the `@` back.
3. **Generic `sk-` keys:** the comment above the token list says the generic patterns need a digit, but the `sk-` pattern didn't check for one. So `sk-learn-and-more-words` was treated as a key. I added a check that requires a digit somewhere in the token.
4. **`MAX_TOKENS=4096`:** this was redacted because a dotenv line counts as secret whatever its value, and `token` matched inside `TOKENS`. I made the name match `token` but not `tokens`, since a plural `TOKENS` name usually means a count, not a credential.

I fixed four bugs in `redact.ts`, and `bun test` now passes (4 tests, 0 failures). The tests are unchanged.

1. **Private key blocks:** the match used `[\s\S]*`, which grabs as much as it can. With two key blocks, it took everything from the first BEGIN line to the last END line, including the text between them. I changed it to `[\s\S]*?` so it stops at the first END line. A block that was cut off before its END line is still redacted to the end of the output.
2. **URL passwords:** the replacement dropped the `@`, so `postgres://app:pw@db` came out as `app:[cedia:redacted]db`. It now writes the `@` back.
3. **Generic `sk-` keys:** the code comment says generic token formats need a digit, but the `sk-` pattern didn't require one. That made `sk-learn-and-more-words` count as a key. I added a check that the key contains at least one digit.
4. **`MAX_TOKENS=4096`:** a dotenv line redacts any value, and `TOKENS` matched the name keyword `token`. I changed the keyword to `token(?!s)`, so plural names like `MAX_TOKENS` (which usually hold a count) don't count as secrets.

Fix 4 was a judgement call, and other fixes would also pass the test. The downside is that a real secret in a variable named `*_TOKENS` (say `API_TOKENS=...`) would no longer be redacted. The other option I considered was keeping the keyword and treating all-digit dotenv values as non-secret instead, but that would leave a numeric password like `DB_PASSWORD=123456` unredacted. Tell me if you'd prefer that.

Some lines of the test file reached me already redacted, so I couldn't see every fixture exactly; the test run is what confirms the fixes. The directory isn't a git repository, so there was no `git diff` to review; the four edits above are the only changes.

export function secretPaths(cediaHome: string, home = homedir()): string[] {
  return ['.ssh', '.aws', '.gnupg', '.config/gh', '.netrc', '.docker/config.json', '.git-credentials', '.npmrc', '.pypirc', '.kube/config']
    .map((p) => join(home, p))

export const REDACTED = '[cedia:redacted]';

const TOKENS: RegExp[] = [
  /-----BEGIN [A-Z0-9 ]*PRIVATE KEY(?: BLOCK)?-----[\s\S]*(?:-----END [A-Z0-9 ]*PRIVATE KEY(?: BLOCK)?-----|$)/g,
  /\bsk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}/g, // Anthropic
  /\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}/g, // OpenAI, DeepSeek and other sk- keys
  /\b[sr]k_(?:live|test)_[A-Za-z0-9]{16,}/g, // Stripe
  /\bgh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,}/g, // GitHub
  /\bgithub_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{30,}/g,
  /\bglpat-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}/g, // GitLab
  /\bxox[abposr]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,}/g, // Slack
  /\b(?:AKIA|ASIA)[0-9A-Z]{16}\b/g, // AWS access key id
  /\bAIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35}\b/g, // Google
  /\bnpm_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}\b/g,
  /\bhf_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,}\b/g, // Hugging Face
  /\beyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}\.eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}/g, // JWT

const URL_PASSWORD = /\b([a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:\/\/[^\s:/@]+:)([^\s@/]{3,})@/g;

// `NAME=value`, `name: value`, `"name": "value"` and `NAME = "value"` where the name says secret.
const ASSIGNMENT =
  /\b([A-Za-z0-9_.-]*?(api[_-]?key|secret|token|passw(?:or)?d|pwd|private[_-]?key|access[_-]?key|credentials?)[A-Za-z0-9_.-]*)(["']?[ \t]*[:=][ \t]*)(["'`]?)([^\s"'`,;]+)\4/gi;

// `token = getToken()`) still reads as written:
// - a dotenv line (`export NAME=value` at the start of a line): any value;
// - a quoted value: 4+ characters for passwords and secrets, otherwise 8+ with a letter and a digit;
// - any other value: 8+ characters with a letter and a digit, and no call or member access.
function secretValue(kind: string, quote: string, value: string, dotenv: boolean): boolean {
  if (/^(\$|process\.|os\.|env\.|getenv|none$|null$|undefined$|true$|false$)/i.test(value)) return false; // a reference
  const tokenLike = value.length >= 8 && /[A-Za-z]/.test(value) && /\d/.test(value);
  if (dotenv) return true;
  if (quote) return /passw|pwd|secret/i.test(kind) ? value.length >= 4 : tokenLike;

export function redactSecrets(text: string): { text: string; count: number } {
  let count = 0;
  let out = text;
  for (const re of TOKENS)
    out = out.replace(re, () => {
      count++;
      return REDACTED;
    });
  out = out.replace(URL_PASSWORD, (_m, head: string, password: string) => {
    if (password === REDACTED) return _m;
    count++;
    return `${head}${REDACTED}`;
  });
  out = out.replace(ASSIGNMENT, (match, name: string, kind: string, sep: string, quote: string, value: string, offset: number, all: string) => {
    if (value.includes(REDACTED)) return match;
    const lineStart = all.lastIndexOf('\n', offset - 1) + 1;
    const dotenv = sep === '=' && /^[ \t]*(export[ \t]+)?$/.test(all.slice(lineStart, offset)) && /^[A-Z0-9_]+$/.test(name);
    if (!secretValue(kind, quote, value, dotenv)) return match;
    count++;
    return `${name}${sep}${quote}${REDACTED}${quote}`;
  });

Behaviour not covered by the tests:
- **Choices beyond the doc comment:**
  - `$( )` and backticks inside double quotes are treated as commands too.
  - Combined flags like `bash -lc` count as `-c`.
  - Wrappers and shells are recognised by their basename (`/usr/bin/sudo`).
- **Known gaps:** here-document bodies, `#` comments, `$((…))` arithmetic and a redirection with no space before it (`cmd>out`) aren't handled exactly as a shell would. In each case the result can show extra commands, but never hides one.
